management_notes: Fred Davidson and team have operated the Royal Mines of Zacualpan Silver District since commercial production began circa 2009 — sixteen-plus years of continuous Mexican silver production. The voluntary temporary suspension at Plomosas (Chihuahua, March 2026) reflects cost discipline rather than a safety or regulatory incident. Management has maintained a strict no-debt policy while accumulating $25M+ in cash, which is exceptional treasury stewardship for a TSXV silver producer. Operations in Mexico require community and regulatory relationships; IMPACT's longevity in-country is evidence these relationships are working.
geology_notes: Royal Mines of Zacualpan Silver District (Guerrero/State of Mexico): multi-vein silver-gold-lead-zinc system with long production history across the Guadalupe mill catchment. April 2026 drill results at the Noche Buena mine (Carlos Pacheco Vein north extension) returned 114.5 g/t Au and 1,295 g/t Ag over 0.61m within a broader interval of 9.79 g/t Au and 212 g/t Ag over 9.49m — genuinely high-grade. The Carlos Pacheco Vein system extension represents real resource expansion potential near existing infrastructure. Plomosas (Chihuahua) is temporarily idle. No resource update incorporating Noche Buena high-grade zones has been published yet.
capital_notes: Public disclosure reports 259,178,650 shares issued and outstanding (sourced from public filings; not from extracted cap-table JSON, which was not available for this ticker). Zero debt. Over $25M in cash as of Q3 2025. Q3 2025 revenue of $10.7M was up 24% year-over-year with the net loss narrowed to $0.6M — approaching cash flow breakeven at the district level. This is a structurally clean balance sheet for a TSXV silver producer: deep cash, no leverage, and a treasury equal to a significant fraction of enterprise value. Warrant and option detail not available in extracted filings.
catalyst_notes: High-grade Noche Buena drill results in April 2026 are actively being followed up on the Carlos Pacheco Vein north extension. An updated NI 43-101 resource estimate incorporating Noche Buena would be a material re-rating catalyst. Plomosas re-activation decision is a secondary wildcard that could restore a second operating mine. Silver prices in 2026 provide revenue leverage to the core Zacualpan production. A resource update and a Plomosas restart decision, in combination, could significantly close the gap between EV and intrinsic value.
acquisition_notes: With $25M+ cash, zero debt, and 259M shares outstanding, the enterprise value net of cash is modest relative to a producing silver company with sixteen years of Mexican operational history. The high-grade Noche Buena discovery adds exploration optionality not yet reflected in a production-only NAV. P/NAV is likely below 1.0x at current prices given the producing district history, cash-heavy balance sheet, and ongoing exploration catalysts. The Mexico jurisdiction discount is real but well understood given IMPACT's track record in-country.
analyst_summary: IMPACT Silver is an underappreciated TSXV silver producer: $25M+ in cash, zero debt, sixteen years of continuous Mexican operations, and a fresh high-grade discovery (114.5 g/t Au, 1,295 g/t Ag over 0.61m) at the Noche Buena mine that could add meaningfully to the Zacualpan district resource base. The temporary Plomosas suspension is a near-term production headwind but does not impair the core Zacualpan operations. The stock offers a clean balance sheet, rising silver prices, and a drill catalyst actively in hand. Watch for a Noche Buena resource update to upgrade to BUY — this is among the cleaner TSXV silver stories for investors who want a no-debt, cash-rich producer with exploration upside.
